chunks: That which the Sheikh — may Allah the Exalted support him — informed me: he said: Abū al-Qāsim Ja'far ibn Muḥammad informed me, from Muḥammad ibn Ya'qūb, from 'Alī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn 'Īsā, from Yūnus, from some of our companions, from Abū 'Abd Allāh (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) prohibited a man from performing istinja' with his right hand.

key_terms.بِيَمِينِهِ: with his right hand — the right hand being reserved in Islamic etiquette for noble acts
key_terms.نَهَى: prohibited, forbade — indicating a prophetic prohibition (nahy) carrying jurisprudential weight
key_terms.يَسْتَنْجِيَ: to perform istinja' (ritual cleansing of the private parts after relieving oneself)

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet Muḥammad (SAWW) prohibit using the right hand for istinja' according to Imam al-Ṣādiq (AS) in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Ṣādiq (AS) reports that the Prophet Muḥammad (SAWW) prohibited a man from performing istinja' — the ritual cleansing of the private parts after answering the call of nature — with his right hand. This ruling, found in the chapter on the etiquettes of acts necessitating purification, reflects the Islamic principle of preserving the right hand for honourable actions, while the left is designated for purification-related tasks.
